decisive_items: Opacification on right frontal sinus, right ethmoid sinus, and right maxillary sinus and expansion of the right frontal sinus and right ethmoid sinus without any bone destruction
High signal on T2-weighted image and ring enhancement in the right frontal sinus
Mild inflammatory infiltrate with fibrosis, lymphoplasmacytic infiltrate, few eosinophils and no sign of malignancy
response.rationale: Chronic frontal sinusitis best explains the sinus opacification/expansion, MRI ring enhancement, and histologic chronic inflammation; mucocele is a close alternative but lacks the inflammatory infiltrate and pus discharge.

rejected.why: No sulfur granules or specific actinomycotic features; chronic sinusitis more consistent.
Histology shows mild inflammation without granulomas, so not clearly granulomatous.
Mucocele typically has more prominent expansion and less inflammatory discharge; histology favors infection.
Lacrimal apparatus not implicated; sinus findings dominate.
No vasculitis or granulomatous necrosis; histology is nonspecific.
